topics: Structural Isomerism Definition & 4 Primary Classes (Ionization, Solvate/Hydrate, Linkage, Coordination)

Ionization Isomerism ([Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Br vs [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄; AgNO₃ vs BaCl₂ tests)
Linkage Isomerism in Ambidentate Ligands ([Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]Cl₂ yellow vs [Co(NH₃)₅(ONO)]Cl₂ red)
quickSummary: Structural isomerism arises from different bonding connectivities. Ionization isomers exchange ligands between inner coordination and outer ionization spheres ([Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Br vs [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄). Solvate/hydrate isomers differ in coordinated vs lattice water. Linkage isomers arise with ambidentate ligands (-NO₂⁻ vs -ONO⁻). Coordination isomers exchange ligands between complex cation and complex anion.
summary: Master the 4 classes of structural isomerism in coordination complexes, diagnostic chemical identification tests, and isomeric pairs.

summaryBox.title: Structural Isomerism Taxonomy
summaryBox.takeaway: Ionization (coordination/ionization sphere exchange), Solvate/Hydrate (ligand/lattice water), Linkage (ambidentate donor atom), Coordination (cation/anion complex exchange).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
DIAGNOSTIC ISOMER TESTS

1. Ionization: [Co(NH₃)₅SO₄]Br (Red) gives pale-yellow AgBr ppt with AgNO₃.
              [Co(NH₃)₅Br]SO₄ (Violet) gives white BaSO₄ ppt with BaCl₂.
2. Hydrate:    [Cr(H₂O)₆]Cl₃ (Violet) precipitates 3 moles AgCl.
              [Cr(H₂O)₅Cl]Cl₂·H₂O (Green) precipitates 2 moles AgCl.
              [Cr(H₂O)₄Cl₂]Cl·2H₂O (Dark green) precipitates 1 mole AgCl.
3. Linkage:    [Co(NH₃)₅(NO₂)]Cl₂ (Yellow nitro-N) vs [Co(NH₃)₅(ONO)]Cl₂ (Red nitrito-O).
4. Coordination: [Co(NH₃)₆][Cr(CN)₆] vs [Cr(NH₃)₆][Co(CN)₆].
conceptBreakdown.content: Review the chemical reactions, precipitates, and color changes used to diagnose each structural isomer class in laboratory and exam settings.

quickRevision: Ionization isomers give different ions in aqueous solution (e.g., AgBr vs BaSO₄ test).
Hydrate isomers differ in number of coordinated water ligands vs water of crystallization.
Linkage isomers require ambidentate ligands (-NO₂⁻ vs -ONO⁻, -SCN⁻ vs -NCS⁻).
Coordination isomers require both cation and anion to be complex ions.
